Hi Samir / Olivia - adding a few technical clarifications and proposed architecture based on your constraints.

Streaming & first-token latency
- Redwood supports token-by-token streaming (SSE/WebSocket) and chunked streaming. For chat workloads we typically target first-token p95 < 100-120ms in the region with an optimized runtime (dedicated pools give tighter guarantees).
- For APAC we expect a ~80-120ms network penalty vs US/EU; to hit your <180ms first-token target in APAC we recommend placing a regional Dedicated pool in SG for the pilot or enabling edge routing to warm KV caches.

Throughput & concurrency sizing
- Baseline recommendation for pilot: reserved Hosted capacity sized to 300 reqs/sec sustained with burst to 1,200 reqs/sec (global) to cover load spikes. This maps to ~150 concurrent model sessions per region assuming average request size ~300 tokens.
- If you expect larger token counts, let us know - we'll adjust vGPU sizing and batching. Expected token throughput: ~90k tokens/sec sustained across the cluster for the baseline above.

Batching / latency trade-offs
- Continuous batching yields unit-cost savings but increases tail latency. For strict p95 targets we recommend a short batching window (5-10ms) and model variants tuned for low-latency (FP16 / int8 quantized where acceptable).

Regional routing & data residency
- Routing policy: we can configure request routing by region via a route key (customer-region header) so EU-scoped traffic remains in EU nodes and logging/trace sinks can be configured to store in-region.
- Fallbacks: for EU-scoped requests we can disable cross-region fallback; we can set fallbacks to other EU nodes only.

SLA differences (hosted reserved vs Dedicated)
- Hosted (reserved capacity): 99.9% availability with application-level latency SLOs we can target in the proposal; Dedicated: 99.95%+ and stronger isolation plus capacity guarantees. Exact SLA language will be in the contract.

Attachments referenced
- I attached a sample test plan and expected latency profiles in the SLO workbook Marissa shared.

Proposed next technical steps
- We can run a 48-72 hour pilot run in the reserved-hosted environment with synthetic traffic mirroring your production mix to validate p95/p99 tail and streaming behavior.
- If results meet your thresholds, we'll produce a Dedicated sizing recommendation for the procurement team.

If helpful, we can include a short runbook for DR/fallback behavior that satisfies your compliance team's in-region processing requirements.

Thanks,
